subject: MAP: FinEx sustained-QPS & token-economics benchmarking — results and next steps
messages:

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Execs want a short MAP that focuses on sustained throughput and unit economics — our main gating items are: sustained QPS at 200 concurrent users (median request size ~450 tokens), TTFT < 150ms target, and predictable cost per 1M tokens so procurement can size the commit.

Can you confirm the tests you'll run and whether you can deliver a short summary by next week? Also include any differences between Hosted and Dedicated for sustained runs (e.g., GPU pool sizing).

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@finex.com>
Cc: Tom Peters <tom.peters@finex.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff + perf targets for PoC

Ayesha — thanks, we can do that. Attached is the MAP + evaluation plan I sketched out (finex_map_summary.pdf) and the raw throughput CSV from our internal run (finex_map_throughput_results.csv). High-level plan: 

- Benchmarks: 3-step runs (baseline cold, warmed KV cache run, and sustained 2-hour soak) using redwood-12B-quant.
- Workload profile: prompt median 450 tokens; expected response median 64 tokens; context length 1024.
- Metrics: TTFT (median & p95), completion latency (p50/p95), sustained QPS, tokens/sec (sustained), GPU utilization, and error/retry rate.
- Concurrency targets: 50/100/200 concurrent simulated users; primary acceptance at 200 concurrent with <2% error and TTFT <150ms p50.

Deliverables by 19 Feb: condensed MAP with pass/fail criteria, cost model (cost per 1M tokens and cost per sustained QPS-hour for Hosted vs Dedicated), and checklist for procurement.

Notes on Hosted vs Dedicated: Dedicated provides predictable per-GPU throughput with autoscale headroom; Hosted uses smart routing and fallback but may require higher soft limits to get steady-state 200 concurrent SLA. I include preliminary numbers below (these are from our lab run, see CSV for time-series):

- Single-GPU (A100 equivalent) sustained: ~18k tokens/sec at median payload (response 64 tokens), sustained QPS ~28 (avg request tokens 514 total).
- 4-GPU pool (Dedicated style): sustained QPS observed ~110 with KV cache warmed (2-hour soak), aggregate tokens/sec ~72k.
- TTFT median: 115ms (warmed), p95: 240ms. Cold-start TTFT spikes up to ~600ms for cold model load.

I'll let Rishi add unit economics, but rough hosted estimate: ~$3.0 per 1M tokens for this model in current pricing bands; Dedicated committed pricing reduces unit cost to ~$1.8 per 1M tokens depending on commit and utilization.

Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finex_map_summary.pdf (MAP + acceptance criteria), finex_map_throughput_results.csv (timeseries), map_benchmark_script.sh (load driver)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@finex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Tom Peters <tom.peters@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: MAP: FinEx sustained-QPS & token-economics benchmarking — results and next steps

Adding unit economics detail so FinEx can model procurement. Notes below are for the redwood-12B-quant workload Hannah ran (median request size 514 tokens including prompt + response).

- Measured sustained tokens/sec (per 4-GPU cluster): 72,000 tokens/sec aggregate. That equates to ~4.32B tokens/hr.
- Cost assumptions: Dedicated committed GPU run-rate used for costing: $12.50/hr per GPU (committed), Hosted effective infra cost blended: $25/hr per equivalent GPU during sustained peaks (includes overhead/ops).

Simple unit numbers (rounded):
- Dedicated: 4 GPUs -> $50/hr; tokens/hr ~4.32B -> cost per 1M tokens = $50 / 4320 = $0.0116 (~$11.6 per 1M tokens). Note: this reflects infra-only; full managed price to FinEx would include platform/SLAs and be higher.
- Hosted (blended infra): 4 GPUs -> $100/hr -> cost per 1M tokens = $100 / 4320 = $0.0231 (~$23.1 per 1M tokens).

Important caveats: 
- These numbers assume >70% sustained utilization during the 2-hour soak. If utilization drops to 40-50% the effective unit cost doubles.
- Quantization and batching optimizations can improve tokens/sec by ~15-25% in some workloads; we can include recommendations in the MAP to hit the target cost bands.

Ask: If FinEx is targeting < $X per 1M tokens for procurement, tell us the target and we will produce a committed-sizing proposal with utilization sensitivity.

Rishi
Head of Inference Performance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick clarification on the numbers above: Rishi, your cost-per-1M-token math looks infra-only and lower than the platform-level pricing Hannah mentioned earlier. For procurement we need the managed platform price including SLAs, monitoring, and fallbacks. Can you produce both infra-only and managed pricing lines? Also can you validate the sustained-QPS target: does the 4-GPU pool you tested map to 200 concurrent users in our profile, or do we need more headroom?

Goal: procurement needs a quote for a 6-month commit by 20 Feb so finance can evaluate.

Ayesha

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: MAP: FinEx sustained-QPS & token-economics benchmarking — results and next steps

Ayesha — short answers and next steps: 

- Managed pricing (platform + SLA + monitoring) for the tested profile: estimated ~$45 per sustained GPU-equivalent hour (this includes 20% margin for ops/support and SLAs). Using the measured tokens/hr (4.32B) that maps to ~$10.4 per 1M tokens.
- On headroom: the 4-GPU pool at the tested utilization hits ~110 sustained QPS (warmed). To reach the FinEx target of 200 concurrent (profile as described) we recommend provisioning a 7-GPU dedicated pool with autoscale + 15% headroom. That projects to ~192-220 sustained QPS depending on request variance.

Next steps: 
1) We will produce a short committed-sizing proposal (7-GPU baseline with autoscale rules and expected utilization bands) by 20 Feb.
2) Hannah -> provide the MAP PDF with the explicit pass/fail checklist and the canary rollout steps (we will include a canary at 20% traffic for the first week).
3) Rishi -> finalize managed vs infra-only unit costs for finance.

Laura
